solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Catch backsliding spouse right away

indicators.note: away means the letter for right is sent off, removed from the reversed word
sliding backwards tells us to read the word for spouse from end to start

parts.note: a spouse is a partner

explanation.surface: Someone's errant husband or wife has strayed and done a runner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backsliding' turns PARTNER into RENTRAP; 'away' removes its first R.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to snare or trick someone into a trap.

clue.text: Midshipman on liner now and then — knockout vessel

parts.note: split as mid plus shipman: the middle letter of shipman, a sailor's word

indicators.note: now and then means only every other letter of the word liner is used

parts.note: a dish is a knockout, a stunningly attractive person

explanation.surface: A naval cadet aboard a ship, occasionally, alongside a knockout punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Midshipman' must be split into Mid plus shipman, whose middle letter is P. 'now and then' takes the even letters of liner, I and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A baking dish for pies is a kitchen vessel, the container one bakes in.

clue.text: Take chair in workplace without one half of seat

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the workplace word goes round the rest

parts.note: an office is a workplace
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: half of the word seat, here its closing pair of letters

explanation.surface: Someone takes the chair at work, though missing half a seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; 'half of' takes the back half of seat.
explanation.definitionFit: To preside over a meeting as chairman is to act as its officiating person.

clue.text: Chaplin thankfully embraced projection

indicators.note: embraced means the letters are held within the words Chaplin thankfully

explanation.surface: Charlie Chaplin was gratefully taken into a film projection.
explanation.definitionFit: The base block of a column or statue juts out, a projecting slab or foot.

clue.text: Peacemakers question male first to establish identity

indicators.note: first puts the male letter ahead of the word for question

parts.note: the UN, United Nations, sends peacekeepers
to question is to ask

explanation.surface: UN peacekeepers want to question a man first to find out who he is.
explanation.definitionFit: To expose or reveal who someone is, as when taking off a disguise.

clue.text: Inconsiderate 'e-man like Peter Crouch — ignore spelling!

parts.note: a he-man is a hunk; the apostrophe drops the H, cockney fashion

indicators.note: ignore tells us to leave out the letters standing for spelling

parts.note: Peter Crouch, a very tall thin English footballer, is spindly
SP is the abbreviation for spelling, as in a proofreader's mark

explanation.surface: A cockney insult aimed at a lanky footballer, with an aside about bad spelling.
explanation.walkthrough: HUNK minus H gives UNK; SPINDLY with SP ('spelling') ignored gives INDLY. Peter Crouch is a 6ft 7in England striker.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thoughtless or uncaring towards others is acting without consideration.

clue.text: A great deal's left buried that is good for the garden

definitions.text: that is good for the garden

indicators.note: buried means the letter for left sits inside the word for a great deal

parts.note: a great deal means much

explanation.surface: Lots of leftovers buried in the ground will help the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A layer of compost or bark spread on soil, which feeds and protects garden beds.

clue.text: A short way to stop sounding dry

indicators.note: to stop means to plug, so the A plus road go inside the word for sounding

parts.note: sonic means relating to sound
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A brief method for stopping something from sounding dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to stop' means to plug a gap, so A and the short way fill the word for sounding.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry humour is wry and mocking, which is the sense of the answer.

clue.text: Where manicurist keeps clippings and equipment?

definitions.meaning: a whimsical reading: a file, a store of records, for nail parings
the emery board a manicurist uses to shape nails

explanation.surface: A beautician's filing system for fingernail trimmings, and her tools.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is both a manicure tool and, read literally, an archive of cut fingertips.

clue.text: Flighty singer's frolic

definitions.meaning: a songbird famous for singing as it rises high in flight
to lark about or play pranks

explanation.surface: A capricious vocalist's playful romp.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer names a soaring songbird and also means to play about mischievously.

clue.text: Four possibly cut off before one or more than one spoke

indicators.note: before puts the station word ahead of the numeral
cut off means the final letter is chopped from the station word

parts.note: BBC Radio 4 is an example of a radio station
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Four, perhaps, was interrupted before one or more people spoke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Four possibly' is BBC Radio 4; 'cut off' trims RADIO to RADI. 'spoke' looks like a verb but is a wheel spoke.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of radius, the lines from hub to rim of a wheel, which are its spokes.

clue.text: Two run-of-the-mill starters take the edge off meal in club

indicators.note: starters means the opening letters of two and run-of-the-mill
take the edge off means removing the first letter of the meal word

parts.note: luncheon is a formal word for a midday meal

explanation.surface: Two ordinary starters take the edge off hunger at a club dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take the edge off' drops the L of LUNCHEON. 'club' looks like a society but is a cudgel.
explanation.definitionFit: A policeman's baton is a short club, a stick for striking.

clue.text: Vandalise nominated play area

indicators.note: nominated means named, so the word is given by how it is called out

parts.note: to vandalise is to wreck

explanation.surface: Wreckers chose to vandalise the playground.
explanation.walkthrough: A rec, short for recreation ground, is a British public park or playing field.
explanation.definitionFit: Recreation ground, an open public space for games and play.

clue.text: Smorgasbord with its cheap ingredients

indicators.note: ingredients means the letters are mixed in a new recipe

explanation.surface: A Swedish buffet made with low-cost ingredients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ingredients' signals that ITS CHEAP is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A medley or hotchpotch of borrowed styles, so a mixed assortment.

clue.text: Half of pubs and small hotels — King's Head included — will offer late session

indicators.note: included means the king letter goes into the rest
half of means only the first three of six letters

parts.note: locals are pubs, in British usage one's nearby pub

indicators.note: small means the hotel word is cut down to its opening pair

parts.note: inns are small hotels

indicators.note: head means the first letter of King's

explanation.surface: Half the pubs and B&Bs, including the King's Head, will stay open late.
explanation.walkthrough: A lock-in is when a British pub locks its doors and keeps serving after closing time. The King's Head is a common pub name.
explanation.definitionFit: Drinking after hours behind a locked pub door is an illicit late session.

clue.text: Wine buff pigeonholed turned out neither grand nor heading for dipsomania

indicators.note: turned out means the letters of pigeonholed are rearranged

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds

indicators.note: heading for means the first letter of dipsomania

explanation.surface: A wine expert, labelled, proves neither grand nor alcoholic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neither ... nor' removes G and D from PIGEONHOLED before 'turned out' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A connoisseur or lover of wines, from Greek roots for wine and love.

clue.text: Mad to live with drunk old yob

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
a sot is a drunkard
a Ted, Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth of loutish repute

explanation.surface: Crazy to share a home with a drunken old lout.
explanation.walkthrough: A Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian dress, seen as a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: Infatuated, so smitten as to be crazy about someone.

clue.text: Possibly retrieve fleece

indicators.note: possibly flags that retrieve is read as get back, the back meaning turned around

parts.note: to retrieve is to get back, and the get is the word used

explanation.surface: Possibly try to recover the wool.
explanation.walkthrough: In effect a reverse clue: 'retrieve' is get back, read as GET written back, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-year-old sheep, or its first-shorn wool, which is a fleece.

clue.text: Chords preceding endless song and dance with verse in that is lyrical

indicators.note: preceding puts the chords ahead of the rest

parts.note: E and F are both musical chords, named by letters

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is removed

parts.note: a song and dance is a fuss

indicators.note: in puts the verse letter inside the abbreviation for that is

parts.note: IE, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Music and dancing with poetry inside makes a lyrical piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the last letter of the song-and-dance word; 'in' puts the verse letter inside the abbreviation for that is.
explanation.definitionFit: Gushing or lavish in praise, which is waxing lyrical.

clue.text: Recycle intermittently? The opposite is solution

indicators.note: the opposite means the selected letters are read in the other direction
intermittently means every other letter of recycle is used

explanation.surface: Is recycling patchy? The reverse is the answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intermittently' picks EYL from Recycle; 'The opposite' turns it round. 'solution' looks like an answer but is a liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: An alkaline liquid, such as one used for soap-making, is a chemical solution.

clue.text: Support for outstanding work

definitions.meaning: aid or help given to people in need
sculpture standing out from its background surface

explanation.surface: Backing for an exceptional piece of work.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means aid for the needy and carving that projects from a flat surface.

clue.text: Standard journalists surmounting resistance

indicators.note: surmounting means sitting on top of, in this down clue above the resistance letter

parts.note: PA is the Press Association, a news agency of journalists
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Typical behaviour from reporters overcoming opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm or average level, as in feeling below par.

clue.text: Sovereign wanting answer is put in danger

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the answer letter is dropped

parts.note: imperial means sovereign, of an emperor

explanation.surface: A monarch short of a reply is exposed to danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sovereign' looks like a noun but serves as the adjective imperial.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger or jeopardise is to expose to peril.

clue.text: Unusual Bellini opera delves into heart of story

indicators.note: delves into means the opera goes inside
heart of means only the middle letters of the story word remain

parts.note: a fable is a story
Norma is an opera by Vincenzo Bellini

explanation.surface: An odd Bellini opera digs into the core of a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart of' trims FABLE to ABL, and 'delves into' puts NORMA in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Atypical or out of the ordinary, departing from the norm.

clue.text: Hell's Angel ringing about Clash

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the about letter goes inside

parts.note: a Hell's Angel is a member of a motorcycle gang, a biker
C is circa, about

explanation.surface: A motorcycle gang member phoning about a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringing' suggests a phone call but means surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: To squabble or quarrel is to clash in argument.

clue.text: Abandon Beethoven's Ninth in ferment

parts.note: to abandon is to leave

indicators.note: Ninth means the ninth letter of Beethoven, not his symphony

explanation.surface: Giving up the Choral Symphony in turmoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beethoven's Ninth' looks like the symphony but is the ninth letter of his name, N.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast or a similar agent that makes dough rise is a ferment.

clue.text: Hotchpotch dish with duck and ginger root scattered in flatbread

parts.note: a pot is a cooking dish

indicators.note: scattered in means the duck and ginger letters are strewn among the letters of the bread

parts.note: O is a duck, a zero score in cricket

indicators.note: root means the bottom, last letter of ginger

parts.note: a puri is an Indian unleavened flatbread

explanation.surface: A recipe: a dish of duck with ginger, served in Indian bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattered in' strews the duck and ginger letters separately through the bread. A duck is a zero score in cricket; a puri is a puffed Indian bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A medley or miscellany of things, like a jumble or mixture.

clue.text: Writer's outwardly no-nonsense pasta

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: outwardly means the outside letters of no-nonsense

explanation.surface: An author appears brisk and practical about pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: Short tubes of pasta cut diagonally, a variety of pasta.

clue.text: Ex Sloaney hairdresser making a comeback — he's a laugh

indicators.note: making a comeback means the taken letters are read backwards
ex means out of, so the letters come out of the words Sloaney hairdresser

explanation.surface: A former posh salon stylist returning to work is a real laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: A Sloane Ranger is a posh young Londoner. 'Ex' looks like former but signals letters taken from inside the words.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal is famous for its laughing call, so it is the one with a laugh.

clue.text: It could be night-watchman is stumped and given not out

parts.note: ST is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped
in cricket a batsman who is not out is still in

explanation.surface: A cricket night-watchman is stumped but given not out.
explanation.walkthrough: A night-watchman is a lower-order batsman sent in late in a day's play to shield a better one.
explanation.definitionFit: A substitute or understudy; the cricket night-watchman fills in for another batsman.

clue.text: When we sit down to eat polenta, for instance, a herb is called for

definitions.text: When we sit down to eat

parts.note: polenta is cornmeal, an example of meal

indicators.note: called means spoken, so the herb is given by its spoken form

parts.note: thyme is a herb

explanation.surface: At dinner we eat polenta and want some herb with it.
explanation.definitionFit: The time of day set for eating, such as lunch or dinner.

clue.text: Stick plug in this place

parts.note: a plug is an advertisement, an ad
here means in this place

explanation.surface: Put an advert right here, then stay put.
explanation.definitionFit: To cling or be glued fast to something is to stick.
